scope: Shared ETF parser preparation: explicit literal versus temporary storage, one-term consumption, charged parsing loops. This does not admit binary_to_term/1.
adaptations: Reuse the existing native-derived intrusive pending-slot decoder rather than executing an auxiliary VM or duplicating term parsing. Temporary storage does not acquire TAG_LITERAL_PTR; literal callers retain existing pointer tags and strict full-buffer checks.

Expose consumed length through the bounded reader so a later binary_to_term adapter can accept trailing bytes as native ETF decoding does. Atom writes and external-fun bindings remain deferred; partially decoded arenas must never be traversed or published.

Pass the storage class through big integers, tuples, list links, binary references and map/HAMT postprocessing. Charge decoder node walks and sized construction/validation loops, preserving allocator/work failure causes independently from parser error categories.

Tests prove a temporary composite and HAMT can be copied into a process, survive arena destruction and moving GC, and retain no literal-pointer tags, including HAMT descendants. Check pending atoms without interning, exact consumed length, every truncated prefix, allocator/quota and work prefixes, and final balance. Independent OTP confirms scalar values, signed zero bits, bytes, maps, trailing consumption and malformed prefixes.

This manifest records parser preparation, not BIF or application acceptance. The subsequent bounded runtime data adapter and its transactional publication/accounting are described in external-sources.json. Compression, fun/resource identities and their additional ownership requirements remain outside that adapter's admitted profile.
